_partNote: Class images for the explorer tiles, rendered at about 74px. Power electronics is mostly small gray blocks, so the seven silhouettes are chosen for outline rather than for detail: a flat tabbed package with three straight leads, an upright can with two posts, a flat board seen from above, a tall narrow case with a toggle lever, a tall finned wall enclosure, a floor pedestal with a hanging cable, and a small cube with folding prongs. Class III is an arrangement rather than an object, so it is drawn as the board the switches sit on, with four identical devices in the square pattern of a bridge. The palette warning matters more here than on any other sheet: busbars, windings, pins and lead frames are all copper or gold in life, and the style override has to forbid them by name.
style: Minimalist technical illustration, the style of a precise patent drawing crossed with an isometric product sketch. Uniform-weight dark slate-gray ink linework with sparse, muted steel-blue accent shading (hex 4E7AA8) on a plain very light warm-gray background (hex F2F3F1). Three-quarter isometric view, single centered subject, generous margins. No text, no labels, no callouts, no logos, no humans, no background scenery, no drop shadows. Clean, engineered, calm. Strictly two colors plus the background: dark slate-gray line and muted steel-blue fill. Every material, including busbars, windings, terminals, pins, lead frames and circuit board substrate, is drawn in that same palette. Absolutely no copper, brass, bronze, gold, orange, red, yellow or green anywhere, even where the real object would be that color. Favor open, airy linework with large unfilled light areas over heavy solid gray shading; the drawing should read as line art, not as a rendered solid model. Draw the subject as one whole object seen from outside. Do not draw a cutaway, a section view or an exploded assembly.

partPrompts.1: A single discrete power transistor package lying on a plain surface, seen three-quarter: a small flat rectangular molded body with a thin flat metal mounting tab standing up behind it, one round mounting hole punched through that tab, and three straight flat leads projecting side by side from the opposite edge in the same plane. Flat and small, the tab with its hole and the three parallel leads the identifying geometry. One object only: no heatsink, no board, no wires, no printing on the body.
partPrompts.2: A single large cylindrical capacitor standing upright on a plain surface, seen three-quarter: a smooth round can of constant diameter, taller than it is wide, with a flat top face carrying two short threaded terminal studs set apart from each other and a shallow three-armed score line pressed into the metal between them. Plain unmarked sides. One object, no wires, no clamp, no board, no printing, and not a battery cell: no crimped shoulder, no raised button terminal.
partPrompts.3: A flat rectangular circuit board lying flat on a plain surface, seen three-quarter from above: four identical small flat rectangular components placed in a square pattern at the center of the board, two short upright cylindrical capacitors standing in a row along one long edge, and a plain rectangular terminal block along the opposite edge. The board is a thin flat slab and the components sit on its upper face. Sparse and orderly, with plenty of bare board showing between parts. No cables, no enclosure, no heatsink, no fan, no dense field of tiny components.
partPrompts.4: A single molded-case circuit breaker standing upright, seen three-quarter: a tall narrow rectangular plastic case, about three times as tall as it is wide and very thin front to back, with one flat rectangular toggle lever projecting from the middle of its front face, a shallow stepped notch across the bottom edge where it clips to a rail, and one plain terminal slot at the top and another at the bottom. The single projecting lever is the identifying feature. One unit alone: no rail, no adjacent breakers, no wiring, no enclosure.
partPrompts.5: A single wall-mounted solar inverter enclosure standing against nothing, seen three-quarter: a tall rectangular sealed cabinet, roughly twice as tall as it is wide and shallow front to back, with a panel of closely spaced vertical cooling fins running down its whole rear flank, a slightly sloped rain cap along the top edge, a plain blank front door, and two short round conduit stubs projecting downward from the bottom face. Tall, slim and sealed. No display, no buttons, no cables, no solar panels, no legs.
partPrompts.6: A single electric vehicle fast-charging pedestal standing on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a tall narrow floor-standing column with a plain blank front panel and a rounded top, a thick flexible cable leaving one side near the top and curving down in one loose smooth arc, and a chunky angular connector head on the end of that cable resting in a holster cup on the side of the column. Tall column plus one curving cable, and nothing else. No car, no parking bay, no ground markings, no display graphics.
partPrompts.7: A single small wall-plug power adapter seen three-quarter: a compact rounded cube barely larger than the plug itself, with two flat rectangular prongs standing out from its back face side by side, and one small oval port recessed in the center of its front face. Chunky and hand-sized, the pair of flat prongs the identifying feature. One object, no cable, no phone, no wall socket, and not a flat tabbed semiconductor package: no metal tab, no wire leads.
